formula: W(F) = F · d · cos(α) ;  P = W/t
sketch:
Observe: SVG canvas showing a person pulling a crate along a floor
with a rope at angle α to horizontal. Sliders: applied force F (N),
angle α (deg), displacement d (m), time Δt (s). HUD: work
W = F·d·cos(α) (J), power P = W/Δt (W). Force vector shown on crate
with cos(α) projection highlighted as a dashed component along
direction of motion. Experiment: reach target power by tuning F and
Δt. Evaluate: HUD hidden; student picks F, α to maximize W for fixed
d, then submits. Wrinkle: cos(α) is the classic 2ème gotcha; "force
perpendicular to displacement does no work" is the discovery.
